historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun described a town named Ajia in his book 'Muqaddimah' which was an important center of trade between the Mediterranean world and the Middle East during the Middle Ages. The town was strategically located near the border between the Christian Byzantine Empire and the Muslim Caliphate of Cordoba.
historical_references.context: Ajia was a significant trading post during the Middle Ages, situated near the border between the Byzantine Empire and the Caliphate of Cordoba.

historical_references.reference: Al-Idrisi, a Muslim geographer, mentioned Ajia in his book 'Nuzhat al-mushtaq fi ikhtiraq al-afaq' written in 1154. He described it as a major port city on the western coast of North Africa, which was an important center for the trans-Saharan trade between Africa and the Mediterranean world.
